## Recall · Lectures 2–3

a) Which part colours the pixels of a frame?
b) A game runs at 120 fps at 720p. About how fast does it run at 1080p?
c) Where does an integrated GPU keep its textures?

::: {.answer}
a) the GPU
b) about 60 fps
c) in the main RAM
:::

## Activity 1 · Requirements · 8 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A store page lists the minimum and the recommended requirements of a game.
- At the minimum, the game runs only at low settings.
- **Do it:** Open the store page of a game you play. Which OS version does it require, and how big is it?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/requirements.png)
:::
::::

## Check 1 · Requirements

What does a good answer show?

::: {.reveal}
1. Google Play shows the version under "Requires Android", for example 8.0 and up.
2. The App Store shows it under "Compatibility", for example iOS 15.0 or later.
3. The OS version on your phone must be the same or newer.
:::

## Activity 2 · Does it run here? · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- We compare each line of the requirements with the same line of the spec sheet.
- The weakest line decides the level of the whole device.
- **Do it:** Enter the lab computer in Spec Check on your phone. Which level does it reach, and which line is the weakest?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/compare-lines.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · Does it run here?

What does the comparison show?

::: {.reveal}
1. Laptop L1 reaches only the minimum, because its 2 GB GPU is its weakest line.
2. Old PC O1 is below the minimum, because it has only 4 GB of RAM.
3. Many lab computers reach the minimum because of an integrated GPU.
:::

## Activity 3 · Which problem? · 8 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A compatibility problem stops the game from installing or starting.
- A performance problem makes the game slow, and the weakest part is the bottleneck.
- **Do it:** Compare your phone with your game. Is there a compatibility problem?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/two-problems.png)
:::
::::

## Check 3 · Which problem?

How do we tell the two problems apart?

::: {.reveal}
1. Android 9 cannot install a game that needs Android 10: a compatibility problem.
2. A game that runs at 25 fps has a performance problem.
3. A weak GPU is helped by a lower resolution and fewer shadows.
:::

## Activity 4 · Five devices · 10 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- 1080p halves the frame rate, and shadows divide it by 1.5.
- Five devices run at 60, 90, 120, 180 and 300 fps at 720p with shadows off.
- **Do it:** Find the best settings that keep 60 fps on each device.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/gpu-memory.png)
:::
::::

## Check 4 · Five devices

Which settings keep 60 fps?

::: {.reveal}
1. Device A stays at 720p with shadows off, and device B turns shadows on at 720p.
2. Device C can use 1080p with shadows off.
3. Devices D and E can use 1080p with shadows on.
:::

## Game challenge · Test devices for Neon Drift

{{< sim file="sims/spec-match.html" poster="sims/spec-match.png" title="Spec Match: test devices for Neon Drift" kind="game" task="Byte Bay needs one test device for each level of Neon Drift. **Play:** match Laptop L1, Desktop D1 and Old PC O1 to the levels on your phone." >}}

## Try it · Sort the devices (harder)

The facts: Neon Drift needs 8 GB of RAM and 2 GB of video memory at the minimum, and 16 GB and a 6 GB graphics card for the recommended level.

a) Desktop D1 has 16 GB and an 8 GB graphics card. Which level does it reach?
b) Laptop L1 has 16 GB and a 2 GB GPU inside the processor. Which level does it reach?
c) What would bring Old PC O1, with 4 GB of RAM, to the minimum?

::: {.answer}
a) recommended
b) minimum
c) 8 GB of RAM or more
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can read the minimum and the recommended requirements of a game.
- You can compare a device with them line by line and find the weakest line.
- You can tell a compatibility problem from a performance problem.
- You can choose graphics settings that keep a frame rate.
